thought.text: All core checks pass. Let me verify config mount integrity and container stability.

reasoning_content:
All core functionality verified. Let me also check the config mount is actually applied (listen :9998, routing behavior reflects config). The routing response shows v2 features. Also verify the config file read from mount — the health shows collabora/llm from config, confirming mount works.

Let me do a couple more checks: the rmeta response Content-Type header Tika compatibility, and confirm the config bind mount contents match. Also check that config.yaml in image defaults differ. But this is sufficient.

One thing to verify: does the extraction actually honor the config routing? The routing came from request features. Fine.

Let me quickly confirm the container is not being restarted/crashlooping and check restart policy, and confirm the config file inside container matches. Then finish.

action.command: cd /workspace && echo "=== config inside container matches host ===" && docker exec workspace-tika-1 cat /etc/open_taki/config.yaml | diff - /workspace/taki-config.yaml && echo "IDENTICAL" && echo "=== restart/uptime ===" && docker inspect workspace-tika-1 --format 'RestartCount={{.RestartCount}} Started={{.State.StartedAt}} Policy={{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}' && echo "=== listening port ===" && (ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep 9998 || curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'health HTTP:%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:9998/) && echo "=== Tika-compat content-type header ===" && curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data 'x' http://localhost:9998/rmeta/text | grep -i '^content-type'
